advances: The untruncated auxiliary law proportional to \(e^{-sQ(v)-|T(v)|}\) has mean endpoint energy \(Q(v)+|T(v)|\) at most \(m_s+\min\{m_s,1\}\). This supplies a finite-radius theorem with an explicit absolute coefficient for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), using the same nearest fiber and the same temperature selected in accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef`. Its sufficient radius margin is \((1+\varepsilon)(m_{s_*}+\min\{m_{s_*},1\})\), in place of that predecessor's \(4m_{s_*}\). At \(\varepsilon=1/2\), the margin is at most three quarters of the old margin for every matrix, and its ratio to the old margin tends to \(3/8\) as \(m_{s_*}\to\infty\). The cutoff coefficient is then \(1/(162\pi)\), with a direct common-point mixed-depth consequence. No bound on the nearest energy \(r\) is imposed. This is a quantitative extension into the finite-radius residual, not a theorem for every \(R\ge r\).
author: research-agent
external_sources: None beyond the results already justified in the declared accepted predecessors. The new Laplace-parameter monotonicity and endpoint-energy estimate are proved in (4)--(5); no positivity or temperature monotonicity is asserted for a hard-truncated Gaussian.
proof:
Positive definiteness ensures attainment of the nearest-point minimum, finiteness of every bounded lattice ellipsoid, and convergence of the Gaussian sums and their polynomial moments. Accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef` proves that the stated \(s_*\) exists, \(0<m_*\le n/2\), and \(\theta_{s_*}/(1+m_*)^2\ge\theta_2/9\). Its parity argument, with precisely the present untruncated weights and the same nearest \(j\), gives \(W\le2^n w_j\theta_2\).

The quadratic identities are \(Q(u+v)=r+Q(v)-T(v)\) and \(Q(u-v)=r+Q(v)+T(v)\). Since \(j\) is nearest, both energies are at least \(r\), so \(|T(v)|\le Q(v)\) for every integer \(v\). Consequently \(\alpha(v)=w_j e^{-Q(v)-|T(v)|}\) and \(\Delta_j(v)=2Q(v)\). In the finite table the two reflected endpoints are retained exactly when \(r+Q(v)+|T(v)|\le R\); on those pairs the original weights and curvature are unchanged. Also \(w_j^{(R)}=w_j>0\).

We establish the new endpoint-energy bound before imposing any hard truncation. For \(s>0\), retain \(M_s=\mathbb E_s e^{-|T|}\) from the proof of accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef`. That proof establishes, for the present \(A,u,T\) and every \(s>0\),

\[
\varphi_s(\xi):=\mathbb E_s e^{i\xi T}>0\quad(\xi\in\mathbb R),\qquad
\mathbb E_s[Qe^{-|T|}]\le m_sM_s,\qquad
M_s\ge\frac{m_s+2}{2\pi(1+m_s)^2}.
\tag{3}
\]

The first inequality concerns the full centered Gaussian law \(D_s\). Its characteristic function is real and at most one. The second and third inequalities are respectively equations (11) and (12) in that accepted proof, with no change of inverse temperature or quadratic normalization.

For a real \(\lambda>0\), define \(M_s(\lambda)=\mathbb E_s e^{-\lambda|T|}\), so \(M_s(1)=M_s\). The one-dimensional Laplace Fourier identity, obtained from the identity used in the accepted proof by scaling, gives

\[
M_s(\lambda)=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{\lambda}{\lambda^2+\xi^2}\varphi_s(\xi)\,d\xi,
\qquad
\lambda M_s(\lambda)=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{\lambda^2}{\lambda^2+\xi^2}\varphi_s(\xi)\,d\xi.
\tag{4}
\]

Both integrals are absolutely convergent, because \(|\varphi_s|\le1\), and Fubini in the first identity is justified by the integrable Laplace kernel. The integrand in the second identity is nonnegative and nondecreasing in \(\lambda\) at every fixed \(\xi\). Hence \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda M_s(\lambda)\) is nondecreasing. Differentiating the defining expectation for \(M_s(\lambda)\) is justified either by the Gaussian first moment of \(|T|\), or by bounding \(|T|e^{-\lambda|T|}\) uniformly for \(\lambda\) in a compact positive interval. Its derivative at \(\lambda=1\) therefore gives \(M_s-\mathbb E_s[|T|e^{-|T|}]\ge0\).

Let \(\widetilde D_s\) denote the auxiliary probability law with masses \(e^{-sQ(v)-|T(v)|}/(\theta_sM_s)\); write \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}_s\) and \(\widetilde{\mathbb P}_s\) for its expectation and probability. This notation denotes only the stated auxiliary law, not a midpoint law or a finite-table Gaussian. We have proved \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}_s|T|\le1\). The second inequality of (3) gives \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}_sQ\le m_s\), and the pointwise inequality \(|T|\le Q\) also gives \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}_s|T|\le m_s\). Thus

\[
\widetilde{\mathbb E}_s\bigl[Q(v)+|T(v)|\bigr]
\le m_s+\min\{m_s,1\}.
\tag{5}
\]

Now set \(s=s_*\). Markov's inequality and the definition of \(L_\varepsilon(A)\) imply

\[
\widetilde{\mathbb P}_{s_*}
\left(Q(v)+|T(v)|\le\frac{L_\varepsilon(A)}2\right)
\ge\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}.
\tag{6}
\]

The cutoff is positive because \(m_*>0\). Every displacement in (6) has both original endpoints retained, since \(r+Q(v)+|T(v)|\le r+L_\varepsilon(A)/2\le R\). It also satisfies \(2Q(v)\le L_\varepsilon(A)\), so it is counted by the finite curvature cutoff. The set in (6) is finite, contains zero, and is invariant under \(v\mapsto-v\). These observations retain the exact endpoint condition, including equality. They do not require retaining every untruncated displacement with \(2Q(v)\le L_\varepsilon(A)\).

Since \(s_*\ge1\), each selected original reflected weight satisfies \(\alpha_R(v)=w_j e^{-Q(v)-|T(v)|}\ge w_j e^{-s_*Q(v)-|T(v)|}\). Hence (6), (3), and the temperature-selection inequality give

\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{j,R}^\Delta(L_\varepsilon(A))
&\ge w_j\theta_{s_*}M_{s_*}\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon},\\
\theta_{s_*}M_{s_*}
&\ge\frac{\theta_{s_*}}{(1+m_*)^2}\frac{m_*+2}{2\pi}
\ge\theta_2\frac{m_*+2}{18\pi}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]

The elementary bound \(\min\{m_*,1\}\le1\) gives \(1+L_\varepsilon(A)\le1+2(1+\varepsilon)(m_*+1)\le2(1+\varepsilon)(m_*+2)\). Dividing (7) by this denominator yields \(B_{j,R}^\Delta(L_\varepsilon(A))/(1+L_\varepsilon(A))\ge c_\varepsilon w_j\theta_2\). The previously cited parity inequality and \(W_R\le W\) prove all of (1).

For the stated parameter comparisons, \(\min\{m_*,1\}\le m_*\) implies \(\tfrac32(m_*+\min\{m_*,1\})\le3m_*=3L_*(A)/4\). Using instead \(\min\{m_*,1\}\le1\) and \(m_*\le n/2\) bounds this margin by \(3n/4+3/2\). Substituting \(\varepsilon=1/2\) and \(\varepsilon=1\) into the coefficient gives \(1/(162\pi)\) and \(1/(144\pi)\), respectively. When \(m_*>1\), the general margin divided by \(L_*(A)\) is exactly \((1+\varepsilon)(1+1/m_*)/4\), proving the asserted limit. None of these comparisons imposes a bound on \(r\).

To apply the geometric consumer, the objects \(w_z,W,\alpha,\mathcal U_j,\Delta_j,B_j^\Delta\) in accepted fact `280b299bc1e87c14` are respectively the present \(w_z^{(R)},W_R,\alpha_R,\mathcal U_{j,R},\Delta_{j,R},B_{j,R}^\Delta\). The table is finite, the central weight is positive, and the selected cutoff includes the central displacement. Its fixed-fiber cutoff conclusion therefore selects one \(x^\star\in C_j\) with \(h_S((j,x^\star))\ge(\ell/16)B_{j,R}^\Delta(L_\varepsilon(A))/(1+L_\varepsilon(A))\). Equation (1) proves the claimed depth bound. This invocation preserves the same point for all containing closed ambient halfspaces, including vertical halfspaces and their boundary mass. Since \(0<\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)^2\le1/4\), the coefficient \(\ell c_\varepsilon/16\) is positive and at most \(\ell/(2304\pi)\), which is in \((0,1/e)\) as in accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef`.

Finally, \(R\ge r+L_\varepsilon(A)/2>0\). For each individual table, choose the parameter \(r_0=r\) in the realization assertion of accepted fact `a7090e5d5aa26b15`. Its hypotheses are then satisfied, and it gives exactly (2) for every positive integer \(d\ge2R\). This use of that predecessor concerns its realization, not its \(r_0\)-dependent depth coefficient. In particular its proof verifies concavity of the radius on the closed ellipsoid, convexity and compactness of (2), nonempty interior, and the prescribed positive boundary-fiber volumes. Thus the new bound applies to actual convex bodies throughout the stated finite-radius range.
statement:
Let \(n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(A\) be a real symmetric positive-definite \(n\times n\) matrix, and put \(Q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax\). For \(s>0\), define \(\theta_s=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}e^{-sQ(v)}\), let \(D_s\) be the probability law with masses \(e^{-sQ(v)}/\theta_s\), let \(\mathbb E_s\) denote its expectation, and put \(m_s=\mathbb E_s Q(v)\). These are the centered Gaussian objects of accepted facts `42cfc4db283237ef` and `a7090e5d5aa26b15`.

Let \(s_*\) be exactly the smallest minimizer on \([1,2]\) of \((1+m_s)\sqrt{\theta_2/\theta_s}\), as in accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef`. Write \(m_*:=m_{s_*}\), an exact abbreviation, so that the predecessor's cutoff is \(L_*(A)=4m_*\). For every real \(\varepsilon>0\), define the new curvature cutoff and coefficient by \(L_\varepsilon(A):=2(1+\varepsilon)(m_*+\min\{m_*,1\})\) and \(c_\varepsilon:=\varepsilon/[36\pi(1+\varepsilon)^2]\).

For any \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), define the untruncated weights \(w_z=e^{-Q(z-a)}\) and \(W=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z\). Choose any integer minimizer \(j\) of \(Q(z-a)\), and retain \(u=j-a\), \(r=Q(u)\), and \(T(v)=-2u^{\mathsf T}Av\). Thus \(T(v)\) is the signed linear functional of accepted fact `42cfc4db283237ef`, not the scalar cutoff named \(T\) inside the proof of `a7090e5d5aa26b15`.

For every finite \(R\ge r+L_\varepsilon(A)/2\), put \(w_z^{(R)}=e^{-Q(z-a)}\mathbf1_{\{Q(z-a)\le R\}}\) and \(W_R=\sum_z w_z^{(R)}\). Use the canonical reflected quantities of accepted fact `280b299bc1e87c14`: in the untruncated table, \(\alpha(v)=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j=\mathbb Z^n\), and \(\Delta_j(v)=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\). In the finite table, write \(\alpha_R(v)=\min\{w_{j+v}^{(R)},w_{j-v}^{(R)}\}\), \(\mathcal U_{j,R}=\{v:\alpha_R(v)>0\}\), define \(\Delta_{j,R}(v)=\log((w_j^{(R)})^2/(w_{j+v}^{(R)}w_{j-v}^{(R)}))\) only on \(\mathcal U_{j,R}\), and put \(B_{j,R}^\Delta(L)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_{j,R}:\Delta_{j,R}(v)\le L}\alpha_R(v)\). Logarithms are natural; all displacement sums are oriented and include zero once. Then

\[
\frac{B_{j,R}^\Delta(L_\varepsilon(A))}{1+L_\varepsilon(A)}
\ge c_\varepsilon w_j\theta_2
\ge c_\varepsilon 2^{-n}W
\ge c_\varepsilon 2^{-n}W_R.
\tag{1}
\]

The original curvature normalization is unchanged: \(\Delta_j(v)=2Q(v)\) for every integer \(v\), and \(\Delta_{j,R}(v)=2Q(v)\) on its domain. Every equality in the finite endpoint condition is included.

In particular, \(\varepsilon=1/2\) gives coefficient \(1/(162\pi)\) whenever \(R-r\ge\tfrac32(m_*+\min\{m_*,1\})\). This sufficient margin is at most \(3L_*(A)/4\), and it is at most \(3n/4+3/2\). At \(\varepsilon=1\), the coefficient is the predecessor's \(1/(144\pi)\), with sufficient margin \(2(m_*+\min\{m_*,1\})\le L_*(A)\). More generally, for each fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the ratio of the new sufficient margin to \(L_*(A)\) tends to \((1+\varepsilon)/4\) along any sequence with \(m_*\to\infty\).

For every positive integer \(d\) and every convex body \(C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}\) whose integer-fiber volumes are \(w_z^{(R)}\), put \(S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\) and \(\ell=-\log(1-e^{-1})\). There exists \(x^\star\in C_j\) such that the single point \(p^\star=(j,x^\star)\) satisfies \(h_S(p^\star)\ge(\ell c_\varepsilon/16)2^{-n}W_R\). Thus every closed ambient halfspace containing this same point has at least that mixed-integer volume. At \(\varepsilon=1/2\), the coefficient is \(\ell/(2592\pi)\). The coefficient \(\ell c_\varepsilon/16\) is absolute and lies in \((0,1/e)\) for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).

The finite tables in this theorem have the convex-body realization from accepted fact `a7090e5d5aa26b15` for every positive integer \(d\ge2R\): if \(B_d\) is the Euclidean unit ball, take

\[
C=\left\{(z,x):Q(z-a)\le R,\quad
\|x\|_2\le\operatorname{vol}_d(B_d)^{-1/d}e^{-Q(z-a)/d}\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
